idiom_name: cats.Applicative: (a, b, c).mapN(f) and traverse over Validated
implementation_notes: Scala has the abstraction as a real type class: cats.Applicative provides pure, ap, mapN and traverse, and cats.data.Validated carries an Applicative instance with deliberately no Monad instance, so a for-comprehension over it does not compile and combination must go through mapN - which accumulates errors through a Semigroup on the error type (ValidatedNec for NonEmptyChain). What replaces the classic structure is mapN/traverse over validated values; Either remains the fail-fast choice. The classic form is justified when a request must yield every field error at once, and it degrades gracefully because the same Applicative interface drives traverse over whole collections.
pitfalls: Validated is not a monad: any for-comprehension or flatMap over it fails to compile (or reverts to fail-fast via toEither), which is exactly why accumulation is possible.
Accumulation needs a Semigroup[E]: with a non-commutative instance (NonEmptyList concatenation) parallel evaluation makes the error order non-deterministic.
traverse over a large collection builds the entire Validated list in memory; prefer a streaming or chunked fold when the collection is big.
The Applicative-only style encourages lifting every check into Validated even when a dependency exists between checks, which forces an awkward conversion back to Either.
